classification_reasons: Spec tightness: the spec is tight. Every flagged concern is decided and the acceptance is measurable. One acceptance item is met by a recorded departure instead of in the diff: the four workflow timeout comments are proposed in evidence/workflow-comments.md, and plan.md was amended in (c) to say so.

Blast radius: about 40 source and test files across the gate (artifacts, checks, gate, limits), the runner (run_phase timeouts and the (e) session cap), auto_round, triage, the PR body, collect.py, init detection, three skills, two agents, three commands and template/sdlc.yaml. Every (c), (d) and (e) gate record gains a `proof` entry and a possible fourth `drive` run, which is a contract that R19 will read. No risk-list item is touched.

Test coverage: the new paths are new code and come with new tests (tests/test_proof.py, plus additions to eleven test files). Each pre-existing test that was edited only gains the new check names, or follows a behaviour change the spec asks for (the ux check's folders). None is weakened.
attempted: Intent: I checked each Proposed-outcome bullet against the diff. All are present: the optional fourth target and its two variables; the drive run by the runner's step at (c)/(d)/(e) and never at (b); drive.log; proof/ cleared before the run; the manifest; the drive kept apart from commands_from_config, recheck and recheck_targets; the time arithmetic (300 s default, 600 s cap at (c)/(d), the (e) subtraction with a floor of 30); the item grammar; judging against the approved plan; the drive-removed park; the image caps; the two folders; /sdlc-test step 3; the verifier step; reviewer angle 9; the PR evidence line; the triage logs; Playwright detection; and the version bump. The change solves the stated problem: the product is now judged after the session.

Spec and plan: the diff stays inside plan.md's 'Files that change'. Two entries were added in (c) and recorded: marketplace.json, which version-check needs, and evidence/workflow-comments.md. The workflow-comment departure is the only consistent route. I confirmed that tests/test_templates.py:334-346 requires the protected .github/workflows copies to equal the rendered templates byte for byte, so a template comment changed alone turns the suite red. The exact lines are handed to the owner, and the arithmetic is in run_phase.py, limits.py and template/sdlc.yaml. The owner should apply those lines in a reviewed PR; this does not block the change.

Proof: test.log, build.log and lint.log carry the deferred mark (the runner's case, not missing proof). gate-c.json's `commands` entry is the runner's green run on db321e6: 2750 passed, 1 skipped; ruff clean; compileall silent. The commits since then touch only the change folder. verifier.md says 'read, not run' and makes direct calls that exercise the grammar, strict_equal, compare_state, the timeout table, drive_from_config/target_logs/required_evidence and the Playwright detection. It names what it did not exercise. The tests in the diff cover those paths end to end (run_deferred_commands with a real drive script, the 127 re-run, no drive at (b), the (d) evidence re-judge, evidence_status). I ignored claude-*.json and run-*.json.

Blast radius, runner step (gate.py:529-669 in the working tree): the drive runs only when it is set and the phase is c/d/e. A not-started drive is re-run through run_targets(only=['drive']), which returns {}, and then run_drive, which clears proof/ first. A crash resets runs and re-runs everything. `proof` is replaced only when the session deferred it. _judge_proof_after fails closed with no `items`, so a step failure is never a round. Records without a drive keep three runs and today's reason (test_an_empty_drive_keeps_today_s_logs_and_verdict).

Blast radius, auto_round: _red_runs keeps every old early return (missing, crashed, deferred, not_started). A failed `proof` entry starts a round only with approved non-matching items and no drive_removed. Otherwise it parks, including when only items added in (c) failed. A red evidence entry on drive.log is accepted through target_logs(True). head_matches now delegates to gitops.only_change_folder_moved, a verbatim lift of the old body.

Blast radius, time: commands_timeout_seconds(config, gate_phase) receives the same gate phase from both readers in the step (run_gate_commands and step_budget). run_caps and run_timeout_seconds subtract drive_minutes only when gate_phase is 'e'. The review pass gets gate_phase='review' and keeps its whole cap. check_limits subtracts the same figure when ctx.phase is 'e'. build_caps_minutes_needed gives 250 with the default drive and 255 at 600, both within 260. Edge I judged not a reason: when drive_timeout exceeds about 95 minutes, the (e) session's floor of 30 makes check_limits park. The runner's step can still run that drive inside the deploy job, which GitHub would cancel. This needs an owner-set misconfiguration that the gate already names.

Blast radius, callers and shapes: evidence_status gains `root`, and all three callers pass it (description bullets, pr/cli.check_run_result, release/notes._evidence_line). limits.py now imports gate.checks at module level. It already imported CheckResult and GateContext from it, and checks imports limits lazily, so no new import cycle. The other `runs` readers (merge_step, digest, failed_runs) read different structures. No guardrail file is in the diff: template/sdlc.yaml is project content, and the root sdlc.yaml, .github/workflows, CLAUDE.md and REVIEW.md are untouched.

Policies: on the security baseline, the drive's environment is drive_env over os.environ, which inside the runner is commands_env(), plus the two variables, with no credential added. Proof paths stay inside proof/: `..` is refused, links are refused through linked_part, and the resolved prefix is checked. The item regex comes from the plan approved at (b) and runs on files capped at 1 MiB. On data conventions, the template comment requires synthetic data, the manifest records the commit and the workflow run, and the record changes are additive. On UX, every new park carries a need text that says what to do. The definition-of-done and ux-conventions texts now match the code.

Tests: could they pass with the bug still present? I checked these cases, and each test asserts the observable value. strict_equal at depth ([true]/[1], {a:1}/{a:1.0}, a list vs a dict). seen 500 on a differs. A dropped image is not produced, with 'dropped' in seen. A stale file is cleared, read-only included. The 127 re-run leaves the first run's file gone. No drive at (b). A missing drive.log is deferred in CI while a missing test.log still fails, and drive.log missing by hand fails. The drive-removed park is never deferred and red_targets skips it. Both stale-proof sides are covered. The (e) floor park is covered. Edited pre-existing tests only add `proof`/`proof_items` to the ordered check lists and extend the ux check for the two folders. This is not a fix-type change.
Skip markers: the gate's ratchets entry lists none (skip_markers []), and the test diff adds no skip, skipif or xfail. plan.md declares none, and none is needed.

Claims against today's code: not an angle of phase (d). I re-checked the claims the build relies on: run_targets(only=...) at checks.py:432; not_started's 126/127 rule at gate.py:404-421; run_phase gate_phase = st.phase for a fix run (run_phase.py:3129) and model_phase=gate_phase passed to compose (:3284); the byte-equality template test at test_templates.py:334. Each holds.

The drive (angle 9): this repository sets no commands.drive and the change adds no project drive file, so there is no drive to check for reading versus writing values. The test drive script (tests/test_gate.py DRIVE_SCRIPT) is a fixture, not a product drive.
